failure_modes.name: Missing_Evidence_Not_Specified
failure_modes.evidence: Summary 1 states: 'No passage identifies who wrote "The Polish Officer (1995)"' and 'To verify this claim, the following evidence documents would be needed: ... Information about "The Polish Officer (1995)" identifying its author'. Summary 2 similarly states: '**"The Polish Officer (1995)" authorship** - A passage that explicitly identifies who wrote this novel'. Neither summary names the specific missing entity (the actual author's name) or the title of a Wikipedia article that would contain this information, leaving retrieval with nothing concrete to target.

failure_modes.name: Insufficient_Retrieved_Evidence
failure_modes.evidence: Summary 1 identifies the gap: 'No passage contains information about H.P. Lovecraft or his genre specialization' and requests 'A biography or overview of H.P. Lovecraft confirming his literary specialization'. The hop 2 query targets this: 'Who wrote "The Polish Officer" 1995 historical spy novel author H.P. Lovecraft genre' (includes 'H.P. Lovecraft'). The hop 3 query also targets it: 'H.P. Lovecraft author genre The Polish Officer 1995 historical spy novels writer' (includes 'H.P. Lovecraft author genre'). Despite well-formed queries naming Lovecraft, no Wikipedia article about H.P. Lovecraft was retrieved across all three hops.

failure_modes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 1 query: 'Who wrote "The Polish Officer" 1995 historical spy novel author H.P. Lovecraft genre'. This is a natural-language question ('Who wrote...') bundled with multiple unstructured keywords, making it difficult for a Wikipedia-title-based retriever to parse effectively.

failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 2 query: 'Who wrote "The Polish Officer" 1995 historical spy novel author H.P. Lovecraft genre'. Hop 3 query: 'H.P. Lovecraft author genre The Polish Officer 1995 historical spy novels writer'. Both queries cover nearly identical concepts (H.P. Lovecraft, genre, The Polish Officer 1995, historical spy novels) with only cosmetic rewording. Hop 2 retrieved Lovecraft's Book, Kulpreet Yadav, The Spy Who Loved Me, Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy, James Moran, Atomsk, and Jacek Komuda. Hop 3 retrieved the same set (Jacek Komuda, Kulpreet Yadav, Lovecraft's Book, Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy) plus Joseph Hone, Pharaoh, Michele Jaffe, Georgette Heyer, Dictator novel, and Spy Line—largely overlapping results indicating queries did not substantively advance.
